text: Whoa, that's hot. But wait, is "spicy" even a taste?
Your tongue can only actually pick out five true tastes.
And "spicy" was never one of them.
It's a compound called capsaicin - and it actually triggers the nerves that sense pain and heat.
So when you eat something spicy, your brain gets the exact same signal as touching something hot.
That's also why spicy food makes you sweat and your heart race - same reaction as touching something hot.
It's also why the unit for spiciness isn't a taste scale - it's the Scoville scale, and it measures how intense the irritation is.
And it's why milk beats water when your mouth's on fire. Capsaicin dissolves in fat, not water.
So "spicy" isn't really a taste. It's pain.
